_comment: Every sound the game makes, in one place. IDs are deliberately EMPTY. Audio assets belong to whoever uploaded them, and hardcoding someone else's id ships a build that is either silent or moderated out from under you. Put a Creator Store id in `soundId` -- the full 'rbxassetid://0000000000' string -- and that cue plays. Nothing else needs wiring: every cue below is already called from the right moment in the client. This mirrors how Data/overworld.json already handles the hub's ambience beds.
_howToFill: In Studio: View -> Toolbox -> Marketplace -> Audio, audition a sound, right-click Copy Asset ID, and paste it here as 'rbxassetid://<id>'. Audio you did not upload is subject to Roblox's audio privacy rules -- a sound that is not public or not yours will simply not play in a published experience, so check it in a published test place, not only in Studio.
_maxConcurrent: Ceiling on sounds playing at once from this system. A full-auto marker against twelve bots can ask for a lot of one-shots in a second, and the cheapest way for audio to ruin a build is to become the thing that costs the frame.
_cues: volume is the cue's own level. pitchVariance is how far PlaybackSpeed is allowed to wander either side of 1.0 -- the difference between a marker that sounds like a marker and one that sounds like a loop, and the reason fire varies more than a round-start sting does.
